 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 Press pass: Major networks suspend White House coverage and 'Trump TV' debuts on YouTube .

 Big milestone: Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) hits $1T market cap for the first time .

 Meta's Muse:  Shopify ( SHOP ) teams up , but Amazon ( AMZN ) blocks from retail site .


 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 Industry shifts 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
 Consumers were closely watching the outcome of the drama taking place over in Hollywood, but there were some other pairs of eyes also watching the movie unfold. Paramount Skydance ( PSKY ) has finally won clearance for its $110B acquisition of Warner Bros. ( WBD ) following a high-profile fight with California Attorney General Rob Bonta and 11 other states. Remember, just a year before this mega-merger, Skydance joined forces with Paramount, combining assets that ranged from production studios to CBS News. By scooping up Warner Bros. Discovery, it's now adding in properties like HBO, DC Studios and TNT, making it a media powerhouse.

 The deal: Given the sprawling assets, concessions with the attorneys general ranged from the Hollywood box office to employment and TV. Paramount Skydance committed to spend an additional $1.5B on U.S. film production and is required to remain in California and maintain physical production lots for both Paramount and Warner Bros. for five years. It also agreed to establish an independent editorial board for CNN and CBS comprised only of journalists with no political bias, as well as promises for movie distribution and independent films.

While that may have settled the scores between the sides, the new content juggernaut on the block is causing alarm among media competitors. Disney ( DIS ) is the primary rival across theatrical releases, linear television, and streaming, and Netflix ( NFLX ) remains a significant competitor for consumer attention and subscription dollars. Amazon ( AMZN ) is also up there with Prime Video and MGM Studios, while the coming Comcast ( CMCSA ) spinoff of NBCUniversal will contain Universal Pictures, Peacock, and other networks.

 What to watch: Streaming rivals will closely monitor how quickly Paramount and WBD can successfully integrate Max and Paramount+, which will make an attractive bundle for many customers watching their subscription count. On the film front, a high number of theatrical releases could flood the box office, but could also prompt cutbacks if they don't justify additional debt burdens. Rival studios may also seek to expand globally via localized content production, or lean on cross-promotion strategies, like experiences integration or gaming and consumer products.
